intro: “Noctuelles” (night moths), marked Très léger, is the first piece in Ravel’s Miroirs. Quick piano figures stop, change direction and break off between phrases, and a slower, darker melody interrupts them.

sections.label: A · Chromatic figures, Très léger
sections.mNote: Quick chromatic figures break off between phrases.

sections.label: B · Song in B♭ minor
sections.mNote: Long chords above a detached bass.

sections.label: Link · Flutter figure returns in low register
sections.mNote: The first tempo returns over repeated bass notes.

sections.label: A′ · Return of the opening figures
sections.mNote: The opening figures return in a shorter passage.

sections.label: Coda · Chords, then a final fast figure
sections.mNote: A Presque lent passage interrupts the quick figures before the close.

cues.title: Opening, Très léger
cues.text: The title means night moths. Ravel marks the opening Très léger, very light. Short chromatic figures pass between the hands, often in double notes, and rising runs take them upwards before a pause divides the phrase.
cues.evidence: Miroirs, Demets edition (1906), Noctuelles, opening page; chromatic figures, double notes and phrase divisions also described by Arisa Tachi: https://enc.piano.or.jp/en/musics/329. Score: https://vmirror.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/e/e2/IMSLP02693-Ravel-Miroirs,DemetsEd.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Dedication and the Apaches
cues.text: The dedication names Léon-Paul Fargue, a poet in Ravel’s circle of friends, the Apaches. Each of the five Miroirs belongs to someone in that circle. The dedicatees include poets, musicians and the painter Paul Sordes.
cues.evidence: Dedications and the Apaches connection: Arisa Tachi, PTNA Piano Encyclopedia, https://enc.piano.or.jp/en/musics/329. The dedicatees are listed at https://imslp.org/wiki/Miroirs,_M.43_(Ravel,_Maurice).

cues.title: Melody in B♭ minor, 5/4 and 3/4
cues.text: The flutter stops. In B♭ minor, a slow melody moves above detached bass notes, in bars of five beats alternating with bars of three. Ravel marks it sombre et expressif (dark and expressive), and the right hand holds a chord.
cues.evidence: Demets edition, p. 4: Pas trop lent, sombre et expressif, 5/4 and 3/4. B♭ minor and the F–B♭ bass are discussed at https://enc.piano.or.jp/en/musics/329.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Autobiographical sketch, 1928
cues.text: In the autobiographical sketch he dictated in 1928, Ravel said that Miroirs marked a change in his harmony large enough to disconcert the musicians most accustomed to his manner. Noctuelles opens the set.
cues.evidence: Ravel’s notes dictated to Roland-Manuel on 10 October 1928, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département de la Musique (Gallica btv1b10073212x, sheet 6): “un changement assez considérable pour avoir décontenancé les musiciens les plus accoutumés jusqu’alors à ma manière”. Our translation. Published as the Esquisse autobiographique in La Revue musicale, December 1938; English in Orenstein, A Ravel Reader (2003), as quoted by Kyle Fyr, Music Theory Online 26.4 (2020), paragraph 1: https://mtosmt.org/issues/mto.20.26.4/mto.20.26.4.fyr.html. Dictation date: Cornejo’s chronology: https://boleravel.fr/wp-content/uploads/RAVEL_Chronology_2018.pdf

cues.title: Return of the first tempo
cues.text: The first tempo returns softly. The quick figure starts low in the keyboard over a repeated bass note, rises, and breaks into fragments of the slower song.
cues.evidence: Demets edition, pp. 5–6: revenez au premier mouvement, low ppp figures and subsequent ascent.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Return of the opening figure
cues.text: After another pause, the opening figure returns at pp. Ravel shortens it this time. The passage moves quickly to the slower closing chords.
cues.evidence: Demets edition, pp. 7–9; the shortened return is also described by Arisa Tachi at https://enc.piano.or.jp/en/musics/329.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Presque lent and return of tempo
cues.text: Presque lent, almost slow. Chords sound over a low bass, marked lointain, distant. The first tempo then returns for a few bars of high repeated chords and a short falling phrase.
cues.evidence: Demets edition, p. 9: Presque lent, lointain, then 1er Mouvement and the final repeated chords.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

transitions.title: A cascade into B♭ minor
transitions.how: A held chord and a quick descending cascade end the first section. The piano moves into B♭ minor, Pas trop lent, and F and B♭ recur in the bass. Over bars of five beats and of three beats, a long upper melody is marked sombre et expressif.
transitions.evidence: Demets edition (1906), pp. 3–4; bass and key discussed at https://enc.piano.or.jp/en/musics/329.

transitions.title: Return of the quick figure over the bass
transitions.to: Link · Flutter figure returns in low register
transitions.how: The slow chords fade over a repeated low note. Ravel writes revenez au premier mouvement, and the quick figure returns at ppp above that same bass. It climbs through the keyboard, interrupted by longer chords from the song.
transitions.evidence: Demets edition, pp. 5–6: return to the first tempo and the low repeated bass.

transitions.title: Return of the opening figure
transitions.from: Link · Flutter figure returns in low register
transitions.to: A′ · Return of the opening figures
transitions.how: Rising runs slow and stop, and a bar at ppp follows. The first figure then returns at pp, in its original position on the keyboard. The two hands resume the light, uneven phrases of the opening.
transitions.evidence: Demets edition, pp. 6–7: rising runs, ppp bar and the return of the opening figure.

transitions.title: Fermata, descent and Presque lent
transitions.from: A′ · Return of the opening figures
transitions.to: Coda · Chords, then a final fast figure
transitions.how: A fortissimo chord is held under a fermata. Quick figures descend through both hands to ppp. At Presque lent, quiet chords sound above a low sustained bass, and Ravel marks them lointain. The first tempo returns once more before the end.
transitions.evidence: Demets edition, p. 9: fermata, descending figures, Presque lent and final 1er Mouvement.

quote.text: Does it never occur to these people that I may be artificial by nature?

composer.background:
Ravel’s father took his sons to factories to see the machinery, and his mother sang to them. Pierre-Joseph was a Swiss-born engineer; Marie Delouart was Basque and had grown up in Madrid. Maurice was born in Ciboure on 7 March 1875, and the family moved to Paris three months later. He went back to the Basque coast many times. Spain appears often in his music, in the plucked-guitar attacks of Alborada del gracioso, the habanera in the Rapsodie espagnole and the clocks of a Toledo clockmaker’s shop in L’heure espagnole.

He entered the Paris Conservatoire at fourteen, studied piano with Charles-Wilfrid de Bériot and lost his place in 1895 for failing to win the required prizes. André Gedalge gave him counterpoint lessons from 1897, and in January 1898 he entered the composition class of Fauré. Ricardo Viñes, his friend since adolescence, gave the first performances of Jeux d’eau, Miroirs and Gaspard de la nuit, pieces he could not have played himself with comparable command.
